source.title: On the Learning Dynamics of Two-layer Linear Networks with Label Noise SGD
source.authors: Tong-Cheng Zhang; Zhan-Peng Zhou; Mingze Wang; Andi Han; Wei Huang; Taiji Suzuki; Jun-Chi Yan

record.file_problem: Text includes the paper through its appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests label-noise training in a two-layer linear regression network and WideResNets on a small CIFAR-10 subset, and extends the analysis to SAM. The versions concern generalization under other interventions and measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-loss and accuracy comparisons for label-noise SGD in Figure 1, plus training/test-loss curves for label-noise SGD and SAM in Figures 2–5. Rows below capture the textual result descriptions; no precise plot values are stated. The pruning result in Figure 1 is about performance after pruning, not the claim versions’ named generalization outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study tests label-noise training and lazy-to-rich learning dynamics, but none of V1–V8. Resampled label corruption is not V1's fixed random-label memorization comparison, and SAM experiments do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors connect label-noise-induced second-layer oscillations to shrinking first-layer weights and departure from the lazy regime, and report similar empirical dynamics for SAM. A qualification is needed: the Phase II alignment and convergence theory switches to noiseless gradient descent and assumes small weights; the convergence lemma additionally assumes perfect alignment. Extensions to nonlinear activations and classification remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies label-noise SGD and SAM in a two-layer linear regression theory and limited WideResNet experiments. Its empirical comparisons concern training dynamics and label-noise effects, rather than the interventions and generalization measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results across label-flipping probabilities τ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} in Figure 1, and contrasts training with versus without label noise in Figures 3 and 6. Figure 6 alternates noisy and noiseless training every 5,000 steps.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 with label-noise SGD has lower test loss and approximately 1.5% higher test accuracy than vanilla SGD across the tested flipping probabilities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resampled label noise can improve held-out performance under the tested ResNet-18 training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Label noise reduces first-layer weight norms and causes WideResNet loss trajectories to depart from their linearized counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise can move networks initialized in the NTK regime toward feature-learning dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM exhibits initial weight-norm reduction followed by alignment in synthetic experiments, and departure from linearized loss trajectories in WideResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can produce dynamics similar to the label-noise-induced transition from lazy to rich learning.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (as stated)
record.problems: The theory concerns regression with a two-layer linear network, while the real-world experiment is limited to WideResNets trained on a random subset of 64 CIFAR-10 images. Generalization comparisons are described without exact values or uncertainty estimates; key curves are shown in figures. The authors state that extending the theory to classification and nonlinear activations remains open.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1(c) reports pruning performance at matched sparsity, which does not measure any listed version's outcome. Figure 6 describes alternating label-noise/noiseless training and neuron dynamics, but reports no listed-version generalization measure. The figure descriptions provide no precise numeric values.

untested.parts: Joint demonstration of fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels, including chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error across widths beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, including training-set size, dropout strength and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no additional results testing V1–V8. States of cannot_determine reflect lack of a corresponding claim-version measure, not absence of the reported label-noise benefit. Pruning removes model components, not V8's memorized training examples.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of fitting random labels with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or retraining comparison.
